note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative (simulated text, fictional commentator, no real citation); no reading of the source is endorsed or ranked.

presets.name: baseline-illustrative
presets.description: Fictional article on notices; the researcher carries R. Ferrer’s index card to passage ¶2, hooks its thread there, pulls the card back across the gutter and pins it in the margin column.

presets.name: contrast-or-alternative
presets.description: Substantive alternative: a four-paragraph fictional rule on filing, a different commentator and researcher, and the card tied to the LAST passage (¶4), so the card travels lower and the thread lands at the foot of the page.

passages: Documents are filed with the registry office.
Each document carries a filing number.
The registry records the day of filing.
A filed document may be inspected by the parties.
sources.commentaryText: Takes “the parties” here to include their representatives.

annotations.text: The thread ends at ¶4; the text of ¶4 is not rewritten

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Long researcher name and role, long source title, long passages, long commentator and interpretation, long references and shelf labels, two annotations.

params.query: article 7 written notice between the parties — commentary

sources.sourceTitle: Article 7 — Notices, communications and addresses of the parties
passages: Each party names in writing a postal address and an electronic address at which notices may be delivered.
Notice is given in writing, is signed by the sender and states the date on which it is sent to the other side.
The sender keeps a copy of every notice together with any proof of dispatch that is available.
sources.commentaryWork: Annotated Notes on the Example Code of Obligations
sources.commentaryText: Reads the words “in writing” in this passage as also covering email messages that identify the sender.

actorLabels.researcher: Legal research assistant, library reading room

annotations.text: The commentator’s interpretation stays on its own card, attributed by name and page
The primary source keeps its own words; nothing is pasted into it
